{
  "claim": "The recovered-from-prose kernel and parse_content function incorrectly report objects recovered from code fences as 'recovered from prose'. The recover_json_object function distinguishes between fence and prose sources (preferring fenced objects), but parse_content always sets the recovered_from_prose flag to True and uses 'object recovered from prose' in the detail message regardless of whether the object came from a fence or actual prose.",
  "expected": "For fenced JSON input like '```json\\n{\"a\": 1}\\n```', the recovered-from-prose kernel should return 'no' (or the detail should say 'recovered from fence') since the object was extracted from a code fence, not prose.",
  "observed": "The recovered-from-prose kernel returns 'yes' for fenced JSON, and the parse_content detail message says 'object recovered from prose' even when the object came from a fence.",
  "reproducer": "```json\n{\"a\": 1}\n```",
  "source_basis": "The recover_json_object docstring states 'The object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one, else the last top-level object in the text'. The parse_content function returns True for the 4th element whenever recover_json_object succeeds, with detail 'object recovered from prose' when there are no duplicates, regardless of fence vs prose source.",
  "execution_evidence": "{\"kernel\": \"recovered-from-prose\", \"input\": \"```json\\n{\\\"a\\\": 1}\\n```\", \"expected\": \"no\", \"answer\": \"yes\"}",
  "scope": "All inputs where JSON objects are recovered from code fences rather than strict parsing or prose scanning",
  "uncertainty": "The documented rule for k_recovered_from_prose says 'prose or a fence (yes)' which ambiguously suggests both should return 'yes', but the kernel name and detail messages imply a distinction should exist."
}
